The **house of Nicolas Flamel** ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _**maison de Nicolas Flamel**_ French: _**le Grand Pignon**_ , lit. 'the Great [Wimperg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wimperg "Wimperg")'[rue de Montmorency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rue_de_Montmorency "Rue de Montmorency") in the [3rd arrondissement of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3rd_arrondissement_of_Paris "3rd arrondissement of Paris").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-M%C3%A9rim%C3%A9e-1)
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=House_of_Nicolas_Flamel&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
[Nicolas Flamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Flamel "Nicolas Flamel"), a wealthy member of the Parisian [bourgeoisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourgeoisie "Bourgeoisie"), commissioned the house after the death of his wife Pernelle in 1397, to accommodate the homeless.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-Mignot-2) It was completed in 1407, as is inscribed on a [frieze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frieze "Frieze") above the ground floor, and it is the best known and sole surviving of Flamel's houses, yet he actually never lived there. The house is probably the oldest in Paris.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-M%C3%A9rim%C3%A9e-1)
The house's [facade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facade "Facade") became a _[monument historique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_historique "Monument historique")_[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-M%C3%A9rim%C3%A9e-1)
The building is currently[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] used as a private home and a restaurant, the _Auberge Nicolas Flamel_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-Lib%C3%A9-3)
## Description
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=House_of_Nicolas_Flamel&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Description")]
[![Ground floor facade](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Auberge_Nicolas_Flamel%2C_Paris_11_February_2017.jpg/250px-Auberge_Nicolas_Flamel%2C_Paris_11_February_2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Auberge_Nicolas_Flamel,_Paris_11_February_2017.jpg)
[![Detail of inscription and door jambs](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Porte_de_l%27auberge_de_Nicolas_Flamel.jpg/250px-Porte_de_l%27auberge_de_Nicolas_Flamel.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Porte_de_l'auberge_de_Nicolas_Flamel.jpg)
Ground-floor façade and a detailed view of its inscription and door jambs
The façade consists of four storeys and has been the subject of successive alterations, particularly during a restoration prior to the [1900 World Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exposition_Universelle_\(1900\) "Exposition Universelle \(1900\)"), when it lost the great [wimperg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wimperg "Wimperg") (an ornamental gable) that had given it its name, and had its windows modified.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-Mignot-2)
The ground-floor layout has been changed entirely except for the three front doors. In the past, both side doors granted access to shops, while the central door opened on circular stairs leading to the upper floors. The door [jambs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamb "Jamb") are decorated with sculptures framed in basket-handle arches, which depict characters holding [phylacteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speech_scroll "Speech scroll") or sitting in gardens. The central door is framed by four musician [angels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angel "Angel"). Two door jambs feature Nicolas Flamel's initials.
Just below the ground floor [cornice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornice "Cornice") is a [Middle French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_French "Middle French") inscription:[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-4)
> Nous homes et femes laboureurs demourans ou porche de ceste maison qui fut faite en l'an de grâce mil quatre cens et sept somes tenus chascun en droit soy dire tous les jours une paternostre et un ave maria en priant Dieu que sa grâce face pardon aus povres pescheurs trespasses Amen
Translation:
> We, men and women, workers living in the porches of this house that was made in the year of grace one thousand four hundred and seven are, each of us, required by law to say every day one [Our Father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord's_Prayer "Lord's Prayer") and one [Hail Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail_Mary "Hail Mary") while praying to God that his grace brings forgiveness to the poor deceased sinners, amen.
